newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Social Democrats gain in April poll.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Social Democrats gain in April poll.

text.p: Voter support for Sweden's Social Democrats, who form a minority government, rose slightly in April from March, a survey by pollster Temo showed on Friday.
The poll, published by the Swedish media, showed the Social Democrats were backed by 31.5 percent of voters, up from 29.5 percent in April and 27.0 percent in February.
But support has fallen from 45.3 percent at the general elections in 1994 because of strict fiscal policies with large cutbacks to the welfare state.
However, the Social Democrats have promised to spend more ahead of elections in September 1998 and the latest poll took place after the budget in which spending pledges were made.
A total 1,014 people were interviewed for the survey.

The main opposition, the conservative Moderate Party, gained more support in April with 32.0 percent of those polled preferring its policies, up from 31.5 percent in March, 31.5 percent in February and 22.4 percent at the 1994 election.

The poll showed that the Centre Party, which cooperates informally with the government, is still losing voters with support falling to 5.5 percent in April from 6.5 percent in March and seven percent in February.
At the 1994 election, 7.6 percent of votes were cast in favour of the party.
